notes: Full description: pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs build_path() at line 272. The security comment at line 269-270 states 'The DFS path builder has worst-case exponential complexity in the pool size. Do not populate the certificate pool from untrusted input without prior size limits. A future version will add a configurable budget cap.' The doc comment acknowledges the risk but provides no mechanism to enforce it. An attacker who can populate the CertPool (e.g., from TLS handshake intermediate certificates) with a large adversarially-crafted pool of mutually-issuing certs (a 'certificate maze') can cause exponential DFS computation, resulting in a DoS. The IDDFS tries depths 1..=10, each with a full DFS. With N pool certs that all have the same subject/issuer DN, the DFS at depth 10 explores N^10 paths. Fix: Add a 'max_pool_size' or 'max_iterations' parameter to build_path(), or add a budget counter in dfs() that returns an error (Error::DepthExceeded or new Error::BudgetExceeded) when exceeded. The doc comment warns callers but without an API limit callers cannot easily protect themselves. Priority: P1 — potential DoS in any application that passes untrusted certs to build_path().
title: FINDING: build_path exponential complexity not bounded, no pool size limit
